name: Question 1
worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =2x$, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡2x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{cos}^{2}⁡2x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x & =\int [5\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}x-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the cos2⁡θ term, given by

cos⁡2θ=2cos2⁡θ−1.

Rearranging, we have

cos2⁡θ=12(cos⁡2θ+1).

Letting θ=2x, we have cos2⁡2x=12(cos⁡4x+1).

Substituting this into our integral, we get

∫(5cos2⁡2x−x22)dx=∫[5⋅12(cos⁡4x+1)−x22]dx=∫(52cos⁡4x+52−x22)dx=52⋅14sin⁡4x+52x−12⋅13x3+C=58sin⁡4x+5x2−x36+C.
